I'll start by reading `TASK.md` and `brief.md` in full so I can follow the brief exactly.The brief is a static Ghidra comparison of stock AF-ON and half-press target records. I'll read the result template and the prior decisions the questions depend on.Prior work names the half-press writer and the AF Button setting, but this task has to confirm both paths from the image. I'll pull those records and hash the inputs before disassembly.The decompiler splits the writer too early, so I’ll scan the image for the real call sites and then disassemble those ranges in Ghidra.The decompiler cuts the writer short, so the next step is a byte scan of the image and a Ghidra listing of the real call sites.The remaining cache reads are in the listings. I am writing the call graph, the zone table, and the sealed result from those bytes.Stock AF-ON and stock half-press write the same ten-byte target record. Half-press is the correct reference. Conclusion (a).

There is one writer, `0x609b3c79`. It reads `0x9a41[0]`, `0x1dd1[0]`, `0x1dd1[1]`, `0x84d1[0]`, `0x88b2[0]`, `0x1df1[0]`, and `0x1e01[0]`. Kind 2 forces position 526. Kinds 0 and 2, and kind 3 with vertical 3, clear the priority byte. A shadow replace from `0xe951` can run first, for every caller. The writer does not read `0x90a1`, pose, custom-slot index, AF Home, or which button is down.

S1 down (`0x610aef37`) stores 4 at object +0x20. AF-ON down (`0x610b962a`, key id `0xb`) stores owner word 2 at object +0x124. Neither edge calls the writer. Both up edges call `0x610a6323`, which does not build a second record. Stored value 0 of `0x90a1[1]` is "Always tracks" (PRIOR T1). Value 1 only skips `0x609025aa` at `0x609024b4`, and that call does not store the record.

All ten zones, landscape and EXIF 6, match byte for byte under that shared formula. Records are `work/result.md`, `work/out/call-graph.md`, `work/out/zone-table.md`, `work/out/listings/`, `work/evidence-manifest.json`, and `work/out/seal.json`.
